1.explanation: The core behavior class LayoutConnectionBehavior listens for connection layout and move commands and updates only the incoming/outgoing connection waypoints. It doesn’t invoke any logic to move labels or text‐annotation associations. Meanwhile, the LabelLayoutUtil utility defines getLabelAdjustment and findNewLabelLineStartIndex—functions that compute exactly how far and where a label should shift after its host connection changes—but these functions are never integrated into the behavior. To fix the bug, LayoutConnectionBehavior’s postExecute handlers must be extended to loop over any labels/annotations attached to the connection and apply getLabelAdjustment/findNewLabelLineStartIndex (via modeling) so that labels follow the resized and re‐routed connection.
1.bug_scenario: After resizing a subprocess the flow’s connection is re‐laid out correctly, but any text annotation or association (label) attached to that connection stays in its old location and “hangs” off the line rather than being repositioned to track the updated connection path.

2.explanation:
• LayoutConnectionBehavior: This class is responsible for reacting to connection.layout, connection.updateWaypoints and connection.move commands, and it updates the waypoints of all incoming/outgoing Connections (e.g. Associations) to keep them hooked to the main SequenceFlow. However, it never touches labels or text annotations. To fix the bug, its postExecute handlers must also compute and apply a move delta for any labels attached to the connection.

• LabelLayoutUtil: Provides helper methods to compute how a label should move when the underlying connection changes. getLabelAdjustment computes the x/y delta for a label’s mid-point; findNewLabelLineStartIndex helps re-attach the label to the correct segment on the updated line. These functions are not currently invoked – they need to be wired into LayoutConnectionBehavior.

• ConnectionLayoutUtil.getConnectionAdjustment: Used by LayoutConnectionBehavior to compute new anchor points for other connections. A similar pattern should be applied for labels: use getLabelAdjustment and then modeling.moveShape or modeling.updateLabelPosition so that labels follow the re-layout.
2.bug_scenario: When you resize a subprocess (or any shape) to which a multi-waypoint SequenceFlow is attached, the Connection itself re-layouts correctly, but any Text annotation or label attached to that connection remains at its old position (“hanging”) instead of moving along with the updated line. Associations (dotted connectors) behave the same: they don’t follow the re-laid-out connection endpoints.
